pages.text: "Not getting up yet..." Bung pulled the blanket overhead. "I was going to serve the first customer..." Little Ddori slept beside Bung as the tied boat rocked.
Mom lit the noodle stove. A line of smoke rose. "Smoke is up, Bung! Morning!" Bung shook the head and shut both eyes again beside Ddori.
Much later, a customer boat was already alongside. Mom handed over a warm bowl. "I wanted to do that!" Bung stamped both feet.
Mom sat by the blanket. "Stretch first when getting up. Arms long, legs long." She held Bung's hands and raised them high.
Bung lay straight on a board, arms stretching up, legs down. With a long stretch, both eyes opened wide. "My whole body woke!" Lying beside Bung, Ddori stretched only arms upward.
Pointing at the stove smoke, Mom sang, "Smoke rises? Stretch! Smoke rises? Stretch!" Bung raised both arms and sang along.
Bung rubbed a wet face up and down with both palms. Drops fell from the chin; cheeks shone clean. "Smoke rises? Stretch!" Ddori raised arms too.
A customer boat pulled alongside. Bung drew Ddori's hand close and stood beside Ddori, offering a warm bowl with the other hand.
Next morning, Bung sprang from the blanket as smoke rose. "One, see smoke? Stretch! Two, splash your face! Three, bowl in hand, to the bow!" Both arms reached skyward.
Mom cupped Bung's cheeks and rubbed gently. Early rising meant not missing a wanted job. Bung pointed to the smoke. "Smoke rises? Stretch!"
